data.long_meaning: The name Ranish is derived from the Sanskrit language and translates to 'Lord of the Rain'. This powerful and evocative name is perfect for a baby boy born during the monsoon season, or for one whose parents wish to bestow upon him the blessings of the rain god. The name Ranish carries the meaning “Lord of the Rain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ranish usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the rain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ranish is a name imbued with the power of the rain god, symbolizing new beginnings, growth, and the cycle of life. It is a name that carries the blessings of the gods and is sure to inspire awe and reverence in those who hear it.
data.etymology: Ranish belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Rain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ranish total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ranish holds deep cultural significance, especially in the Hindu tradition. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra is the god of rain, thunderstorms, and the sky. The onset of the monsoon season is believed to be under his influence. By choosing the name Ranish, parents are invoking the blessings of Lord Indra and acknowledging the power and importance of rain in agricultural societies.
data.spiritual_significance: On a more spiritual level, the name Ranish carries the energy and essence of abundance, renewal, and transformation. The monsoon rains bring life-giving water to parched lands, resulting in new growth and nourishment. This name symbolizes the idea of giving and receiving, and serves as a reminder of the cyclical nature of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ranish is believed to resonate with the divine qualities of courage, leadership, and wisdom. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ran' meaning courage and 'Is' meaning ruler or leader. This name inspires one to embrace challenges with valor, make informed decisions with wisdom, and lead a fearless, virtuous life.

historical_references.reference: Ranish was a Hindu king of the Vakataka dynasty who ruled over the Deccan plateau in southern India between 480 to 510 AD. He is known for his military campaigns against the Kalabhra kings in the northern Deccan and the Chalukyas in the eastern Deccan.

Ranish is also mentioned in the Sanskrit epic 'Mahabharata' as the name of a king of the Anga kingdom in eastern India who ruled during the Mahabharata war around 3000 BC. This Ranish is not to be confused with the Ranish of the Vakataka dynasty.
